prayerExcerpt.en-US: If as a Christian, let him not be ashamed, but let him glorify God in that name.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Se padecer como cristão, não se envergonhe, antes glorifique a Deus nesse nome.

meta.face: Seven clearly different North Africans of the Roman province, warm olive-brown to deep-brown skin. LIBERATUS (centre front), the abbot, about sixty-five: a LARGE, BOXY head with a flat crown — a broad, deeply lined forehead, a strong ROMAN nose with a high bridge, grave, HOODED dark-brown eyes, deep lines from nose to mouth, a thin, wide mouth, a SQUARE chin under a short, full WHITE beard cut square; close white hair. MAXIMUS (front, at his right), a boy of about twelve, the darkest-skinned of the group, deep brown: a soft OVAL face with full cheeks, a BROAD, short nose with wide nostrils, very LARGE dark eyes, a full mouth, a softly rounded chin; black hair in short, tight curls close to the head; looking up at his abbot. Not the triangular, big-eared Vitalis or the chubby Martialis of seven_brothers. BEHIND, left to right: BONIFACE, about forty, a ROUND, full face with a short black beard and a broad, kind smile; SERVUS, about thirty, a LONG, NARROW, beardless face with a hooked nose; RUSTICUS, about thirty-five, a BROAD, FLAT face with a snub nose and dark stubble, thick black hair; ROGATUS, about fifty-five, GAUNT, bald on the crown, with a wispy grey beard; SEPTIMUS, about forty-five, a PEAR-SHAPED face, heavy in the jaw, clean-shaven, with short, thick grey-black hair. All gazes calm, some lifted.
meta.basis: No likeness survives; Victor of Vita's account, which the book follows, gives only their names, the monastery near Capsa and the boy Maximus's youth. The faces are ours, seven different men and a boy of Roman Africa.
